prompt: A bag contains 5 red and 3 blue counters. Two are taken without replacement. Find the probability that they are different colours.
markscheme:
$P(RB)+P(BR)=\dfrac58\cdot\dfrac37+\dfrac38\cdot\dfrac57$ **(M1)(A1)** $=\dfrac{30}{56}=\dfrac{15}{28}$ **(A1)**

Without replacement, the second-stage probabilities have denominator 7.

prompt:
$P(A)=0.5$, $P(B)=0.4$ and $P(A\cup B)=0.7$.

**(a)** Find $P(A\cap B)$. **[2]**

**(b)** Determine whether $A$ and $B$ are independent. **[1]**
$A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive events with $P(A)=0.3$ and $P(B)=0.4$. Explain why $A$ and $B$ cannot be independent.
markscheme: Mutually exclusive: $P(A\cap B)=0$ **(A1)**. Independence would need $P(A\cap B)=0.3\times0.4=0.12\ne0$. Knowing $A$ happened tells you $B$ did not, so they are dependent **(R1)**

prompt:
| | Walk | Bus | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Year 10 | 30 | 20 | 50 |
| Year 11 | 15 | 35 | 50 |

A student is chosen at random. Find

**(a)** $P(\text{Bus}\mid\text{Year 11})$ **[1]**

**(b)** $P(\text{Year 11}\mid\text{Bus})$ **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $\dfrac{35}{50}=0.7$ **(A1)**

**(b)** The condition restricts to the 55 bus users **(M1)**: $\dfrac{35}{55}=\dfrac{7}{11}$ **(A1)**

$P(A\mid B)$ and $P(B\mid A)$ are generally different — the denominators are different groups.
